newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWF raises forecast for Australian barley.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWF raises forecast for Australian barley.

text.p: Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty Ltd (AWF) has increased its forecast for Australia's 1996/97 (April-March) barley production to 5.96 million tonnes from its previous forecast of 5.51 million tonnes.
Weather had been cool in all areas and crops sent out plenty of tillers, AWF said in its sixth barley forecast.
Rain and cool weather had enabled crops in all areas to make steady progress without being set back by soil water stress, AWF said.
Steady crop growth was expected to result in higher percentages of the grain in each state being assessed as malting quality, AWF said.
However, any prolonged heat wave conditions before the crop was ripe could counter current prospects for malting segregations, it said.
The Queensland crop was the best for several years and signalled a welcome departure of drought conditions from the state, it said.
Crops in New South Wales were able to be sown as early as May and had enjoyed excellent growing conditions since, it said.
After application of additional fertiliser, crops were very thick. AWF was forecasting an average yield of 2.15 tonnes per hectare for Queensland.
Strong northerly winds had caused great concern about stress on more advanced crops, it said.
Over the past 14 days only eight millimetres of rain fell in NSW barley areas, in the Riverina district. However, rain was forecast before the end of the present week.
Victorian and South Australian crops were both late and behind in maturity,it said. Yield prospects in both states are excellent, it said.
"We would expect the wheat harvest to start well before any barley is stripped," AWF managing director Brian Bailey said.
The area sown in Western Australia is down on last year and well down on the area growers intended to sow, AWF said.
Conditions were first too dry for cultivation, then they quickly became too wet for tractors to operate, it added.
